reference_uncertainties.detail: The judgment reports governmental offer, Lime Co. acceptance, trial recognition and High Court recognition of an agreement. The complete original communications and draft instruments are unavailable. Section 7's unqualified-acceptance condition therefore supports conditional analysis, without requiring a definitive independent finding about unproduced words.

Reported agreement, physical entry, draft instruments, statutory execution and registration must remain distinct. The source materials do not provide the complete executed lease instruments or authorization resolutions.

The Government's 1934 forfeiture, Kuchwar's successful prior litigation, the separate contempt reversal, failed restitution and Kuchwar's 1948 expiration are distinguishable. Neither the contested original forfeiture nor reversal of contempt automatically establishes an unrestricted 1934 grant to Lime Co.

reference_uncertainties.issue: Government ownership versus immediate power to lease
reference_uncertainties.detail: S830e8b76ae83 describes the Government as owner, while Kuchwar held pre-existing lease rights. S4da221281e65 reports the High Court's section 20 mutual-mistake conclusion about governmental title. Whether the asserted problem constituted a shared mistake of essential fact remains contested.

The reported April 1934 effective date and trial finding of commencement upon execution cannot be automatically reconciled. The actual execution date is not established, Kuchwar's lease continued until March 1948, and the later alternative request began April 1949.

The draft mistake issue was deleted, and the quoted procedural record reports no corresponding defense allegation. These facts do not by themselves establish whether the High Court could legally address mistake, because the applicable full procedural framework and target reasoning are unavailable.

Section 30's excerpt requires execution by an authorized person in an authorized manner for contracts within its scope. The High Court found noncompliance, but the complete statutory setting, authorizing resolution and primary execution evidence are not supplied.

The available case material reports the plaintiff's reliance and the High Court's reconstruction objection. The operative section 18(a) text is absent. A reference must not demand additional unprovided statutory requirements or a definitive target-court answer.

The written application says the plaintiff relinquishes all claims to further performance, followed by compensation language with a cutoff before April 1948. It is not sufficiently clear from the supplied excerpt whether the cutoff limits the performance clause, the compensation clause, or both. Preserve this textual scope uncertainty.

The written release refers to compensation before April 1948, the oral clarification refers to periods before execution, and the requested alternative begins April 1949 while retaining permissible compensation. The possible gap and the procedural effect of oral clarification remain unresolved.

Further-performance relinquishment and compensation relinquishment are independent substantive obligations. Accurate reporting of the written or oral language does not itself establish legal sufficiency, especially without the operative section 15 text.

The High Court rejected readiness and willingness and independently declined discretionary relief. The legal significance of a later narrowed claim is open. Neither historical finding may be automatically adopted as the target court's conclusion.

Transmission, requested production and nonproduction are recorded. The exact contents, permitted inference from nonproduction and any procedural consequences are not fully established. A negative evidentiary inference must be supported separately if asserted.

Dalmia contested corporate existence and standing; the trial court rejected that objection; the High Court found Lime Co. was not the real plaintiff. The available excerpts do not identify a substitute real claimant or provide sufficient underlying evidence to resolve the objection independently.

Dalmia claimed leasehold rights for consideration; the trial court found a one-year lease with notice and denied Dalmia locus to contest specific performance. These are attributed positions and findings, not definitive proof of later-lessee liability or ultimate priority.

Limitation, estoppel, acquiescence and waiver were pleaded and rejected at trial. Complete factual foundations and limitation calculations are absent. General waiver defenses, section 15 relinquishment and statutory waiver of earlier lease forfeiture remain separate.

The trial decree specified a compensation period but reserved quantification. The independent breach-damages route under section 73 remains conditional on an applicable contractual obligation, breach, loss and statutory recovery limits. The record supplies no adequate basis for quantification or unconditional entitlement.

The trial and High Court conclusions are established as attributed historical positions. The target appellate court's reasons, treatment of each ground and ultimate disposition are withheld. No proposed item requires recovering or predicting them.

reference_limitations: This is a complete source-only model item-design proposal, not audited human gold, legal certification, experimental evaluation or a determination of the withheld appeal. All 74 proposed items have equal binary weight and represent distinct material relations or independently necessary legal questions. A positive item requires accurate actors, properties, stages, polarity and legally necessary conditions; equivalent language is acceptable. An OPEN item can be satisfied through identification of its specific source-supported unresolved reason and must not require a hidden judgment or unsupported legal conclusion. Attributed historical findings and independent legal application are scored separately where independently material. No criterion is self-triggered merely because a report mentions an optional statutory theory; optional doctrines require a supported nexus before their application can be assessed. The source excerpts are judgment reports, not original exhibits. The available LAW provisions do not establish universal historical applicability. The original executed instruments, complete drafts, authorizing resolutions, full sections 15 and 18(a), damages proof, relevant missing procedural rules and target appellate reasoning are unavailable. The three identified quotation mismatches have been repaired by exact contiguous source witnesses or correct source-fragment attribution; mechanical quotation errors have not been treated as substantive invalidity. No evaluated reports, system identities, methods, scores, hidden dispositions, case memory or external sources were used.
